input.headline: Last week went to plan: every run landed within a tenth of a mile of the distance planned, and the marathon-pace session ran at the right effort. This week keeps building gently with 43 miles, a 16 mile long run, and no doubling of volume.
input.analysis:
## What the week showed

Every planned run was done, and both rest days were taken. The distances matched the plan within a tenth of a mile, so the week ran the way it was meant to.

The marathon-pace session was the key work. The middle of the run sat between 8:30 and 8:40 per mile, close to the 8:35 pace a 3:45 marathon needs. You ran the effort asked for, not faster.

The easy days were well controlled. They averaged a heart rate of 139 at about 9:50 per mile, compared with 151 at 10:28 in the hot weeks of late August. Your easy running is getting more efficient.

The one gap was easy share, at 64 percent against a target of 80 percent. The 15 mile long run averaged a heart rate of 146 and drifted up about 6 beats, so a little over half its time sat in zone 3. That is a normal result for a long run, but it is why the easy share came in low.

## Volume and the next block

| Week | Miles | Long run | Easy share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sep 7 – 13 | 53 | 20 mi | 54% |
| Sep 14 – 20 | 40 | 15 mi | 64% |
| Sep 21 – 27 (planned) | 43 | 16 mi | 80% target |

Volume should rise slowly from here. This week's 43 miles is about 8 percent more than last week, and the long run adds one mile. That keeps the load steady after the spike of the week of Sep 7.

This week's quality session is threshold work, because the build phase adds threshold running and last week already covered marathon pace. The Thursday medium-long run adds aerobic time without adding intensity, which is what a marathon build needs. Keep it conversational so it does not turn into a second hard day.

Marathon-pace segments will come into a long run in the weeks ahead, once the easy share is back near 80 percent. Plan a lighter week in three or four weeks, then taper in the final stretch before Nov 1.
input.answers:
No, I would not double to 80 miles, and I would not run twice a day. Going from about 40 miles to 80 is a doubling, and a safe weekly increase is closer to 10 percent.

Your club mate's 70 miles is built over years of training. It is not a starting point for you, and matching it now would add fatigue and injury risk in the last five weeks before the race.

The week of Sep 7 reached 53 miles with a 20 mile long run, which was more than the plan asked. This week's plan is 43 miles, and a peak near 50 miles is a sensible ceiling for your marathon.

If you feel you have missed miles, let them go. Consistent easy running now will do more for your 3:45 than catching up.
input.flags:
Easy share below target: 64 percent of last week's time was in zones 1 and 2, against 80 percent. Keep Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday under the heart rate limits in the plan so the easy days stay easy.
Long run drift: the 15 miler averaged 146 and climbed to about 151. Start the 16 miler at 10:00 per mile or slower and let the heart rate settle before the middle miles.
Threshold reps: stop at three. Hold about 8:00 per mile on each rep. In the week of Sep 7 an extra rep was added and the pace ran faster than planned.
Weekly volume: keep it near 43 miles. The week of Sep 7 reached 53 miles with a 20 mile long run, and that spike should not repeat.</flags>
<parameter name="plan">Mon 2026-09-21: rest. Full rest after the 15 mile long run lets the legs absorb the work before the week's quality session.
Tue 2026-09-22: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 140, flat route. Keeps the easy days truly easy so the week gets closer to the 80 percent easy target.
Wed 2026-09-23: quality, 8 mi: 2 mi easy, 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00 per mile with 2 min easy jog between, 1.5 mi easy. Stop at three reps even if you feel strong. Threshold work is the build focus, and three controlled reps keep the effort right before the long run.
Thu 2026-09-24: easy, 8 mi, heart rate under 145, conversational pace. The midweek medium-long run adds aerobic time on tired legs without adding intensity.
Fri 2026-09-25: rest. A full day off keeps the weekend long run fresh and protects the build.
Sat 2026-09-26: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 140. A short easy run on tired legs builds weekly volume gently ahead of the long run.
Sun 2026-09-27: long, 16 mi, heart rate under 150, start at 10:00 per mile or slower. One mile more than last week's 15, kept aerobic; marathon-pace segments come in a later long run.
